newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia truckers' strike virtually over - union.
newsitem.headline: Colombia truckers' strike virtually over - union.

text.p: A six-day-old strike by Colombia's main truck drivers' union is likely to end sometime early Friday, union officials and government negotiators said.
"It's likely to happen within a few hours," said union leader Javier Suarez, when asked how soon the crippling work stoppage might be lifted.

"We're still working out a few points but everything is basically agreed," Suarez told Reuters, adding that the union would wait until President Ernesto Samper had signed a final accord, hammered out during more than 19 hours of talks at the Transportation Ministry, before rank-and-file members of Colombian Truck Drivers' Association (ACC) were actually ordered back to work.
"We don't trust anyone," Suarez said, stressing that agreements worked out at the bargaining table would not be taken on face value until they were endorsed by Samper himself.

The strike was called by the ACC, which represents 80 percent of Colombia's truckers, on grounds that government officials and private transportation companies had failed to fulfill terms of an agreement that ended an 11-day strike in October.
